_about: THE FAMILY LIBRARY: every kind of object the asset maker knows how to make, and how. Your AI looks at the picked photo and decides which family an item belongs to (library/families.py). The family then decides everything that follows: which sides to hunt, which facts to look up, how it is made in a factory (the recipe), which builder makes it, and which exact checks it must pass. A family whose builder does not exist yet sends the item to the general one-off builder (parts), never to a wrong builder - nothing is ever faked onto a box. builder_status: ready = proven on real items; partial = works but known gaps (listed); missing = no builder yet.

folding_carton.what: a printed paperboard box folded from one flat sheet, with tuck or glued flaps
looks_like: toy or game box made of thin card
judge_notes: every side printed edge to edge like the real carton
flaps and creases where the real carton has them
the barcode on the side the real carton has it

zones.name: back
typical: a promotion, game, recipe or product story of that era

zones.name: left
typical: the Nutrition Facts panel (in that year's format)

zones.name: right
typical: the maker's 'distributed by' name and address

zones.name: top
typical: the brand logo and product name on the flap

rigid_case.what: a hard plastic case or clamshell that holds media or a product
gaps: built as a solid block: no hinge, no hollow inside, no clear sleeve over the printed insert

media_cartridge.what: a tape or cartridge: a molded plastic shell with a label and moving parts inside
not: the case it is sold in
gaps: built from parts by the general builder until a cassette/VHS shell builder exists

printed_circuit_card.what: an electronic circuit board with chips and parts on it
not: a device with a plastic shell around the board
gaps: chips are boxes with the photo on top (no leads/pins)
the solder side is made up
the bracket is a flat plate
judge_notes: gold fingers read as gold metal
the bracket reads as bent steel

looks_like: 9-volt is NOT this (it is a box shape)
judge_notes: the label covers the can completely and rolls over both shoulders: no bare steel ring showing outside the label
the + end is a raised steel button
a thin overlap seam runs down the side

AA.source: IEC 60086-2 LR6 (the measured AA master spec)

AAA.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AAA_battery (IEC LR03): 10.5 x 44.5 mm, button max 3.8 mm across, min 0.8 mm high

C.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_battery: 26.2 x 50 mm (button not given: scaled from the AA)

D.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D_battery: nominal 33.2 x 61.5 mm (button not given: scaled from the AA)

zones.name: label
typical: a date code or 'best if installed by' date
a + mark at the plus end
any tester or feature of that era (e.g. a PowerCheck strip with test dots)

zones.name: top
typical: bare plated steel with the raised + button and pressed rings

zones.name: bottom
typical: bare plated steel, flat, with pressed rings

beverage_can.what: a drawn aluminum or steel can for drinks or food
not: a paint can with a lid
gaps: no pull tab or countersink detail yet

12 fl oz.source: Can Manufacturers Institute 202 can standard (cancentral.com): body 2.602 in across, flange height 4.812 in; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drink_can: 4.83 in high, 2.13 in across at the lid, 2.6 in at the body

zones.name: label
typical: the brand logo (often twice, opposite sides)
the maker's or bottler's name and address
a recycling / deposit line (e.g. CA CASH REFUND, ME 5¢)

zones.name: top
typical: bare aluminum lid with the pull tab and score line

zones.name: bottom
typical: bare aluminum dome, sometimes an ink-jet date code

bottle_or_jar.what: a bottle or jar with a cap or lid
gaps: cap, body and label are separate parts only when the profile is traced in parts
glass and clear plastic are not see-through yet

flexible_wrapper.what: a thin sealed wrapper or pouch around a product (crimped or pillow-sealed ends)
gaps: built from parts by the general builder until a pillow-pack builder exists

soft_bag.what: a fabric or vinyl bag, often zippered, sometimes holding a kit
gaps: built from parts by the general builder (body, zipper, handle, contents)

molded_device.what: a gadget or toy with a hard molded plastic shell, buttons and parts
gaps: built from parts by the general builder; organic curves need the organic builder (Hunyuan)
needs the organic builder (Hunyuan) working on this Mac, plus cloth thickness and seams
needs the organic builder (Hunyuan), then sole / upper / laces as separate parts

organic_toy.what: a toy or figure with soft or sculpted organic shapes
gaps: needs the organic builder (Hunyuan) working on this Mac

flat_printed.what: a thin printed sheet or card

general.what: anything that fits no other family: a one-off, built from its parts
gaps: simple shapes (boxes, cylinders, spun profiles, sheets, tubes) are built from the photo; organic parts need the organic builder (Hunyuan)

_side_words: side_words: how collectors and sellers name each side of this kind of thing in a search (the dossier's hunt uses them instead of box words)
_zone_elements: zones[].elements: what a rebuilt zone draws from facts with receipts (eraprint: logo, name, picture, net_weight, maker_lines, legal_lines, nutrition, ingredients, upc), in order; zones[].typical: the same in words, for your AI when it rebuilds artwork (kits.py)
